quizName: DMV Practice Test #5 25 Questions • Passing Score 21

questions.question: Where is a motorcycle most likely to have a conflict with other vehicles?
questions.explanation: Intersections are where most motorcycle conflicts happen. Stay alert and watch for vehicles that may cross your path.

questions.question: Which factor does NOT affect blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
questions.explanation: BAC is affected by how much alcohol you drink, how fast you drink it, and your body weight. Height does not affect BAC.

questions.question: What percentage of a motorcycle's total braking power comes from the front brake?
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides most of the motorcycle's stopping power.

questions.question: What should you do to make yourself more visible on a motorcycle?

options.text: Turn off your headlight during the day.
Keep your headlight on at all times.
Ride in the right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your headlight on at all times.
questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on at all times. Also wear bright or reflective clothing and change your lane position as needed to stay visible.

questions.question: How often should you check your mirrors while riding a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors frequently to stay aware of what is behind you and spot potential hazards.

questions.question: Which of the following will NOT reduce your chance of serious injury in a crash?
questions.explanation: Wear an approved helmet, face or eye protection, and protective clothing to reduce injury. A windshield does not provide significant protection in a crash.

questions.question: Which sign is rectangular?
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular with white backgrounds and black lettering. These signs show rules you must follow.

questions.question: When riding downhill on a motorcycle with a sidecar, how does stopping compare to riding without a sidecar?

options.text: Stopping will be easier than when riding without a sidecar.
Stopping will take longer than when riding without a sidecar.
Stopping is about as easy as it is when riding without the sidecar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stopping will take longer than when riding without a sidecar.
questions.explanation: A sidecar adds weight to your motorcycle. Extra weight makes stopping harder and takes longer, especially downhill.

questions.question: When braking a motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Only use the rear brake on slippery surfaces, such as wet pavement.

questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop, no matter what the road conditions are.

questions.question: What color is a warning sign?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert you to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger in a sidecar, what should you do?

options.text: Start slowing down sooner than usual.
Start slowing down later than usual.
Brake harder than usual to stop quickly.
Brake gently to avoid wearing out the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Start slowing down sooner than usual.
questions.explanation: The extra weight of a passenger in a sidecar changes how your motorcycle handles. You will need more distance to stop completely.

questions.question: Why should you avoid riding alongside another motorcyclist?

options.text: It allows you to use more of the road.
It limits your escape routes if something goes wrong.
It lets you communicate with the other rider.
It makes it easier for other drivers to pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: It limits your escape routes if something goes wrong.
questions.explanation: Riding side-by-side with another motorcyclist limits both riders' ways to escape if a hazard appears.

questions.question: Where is the gear shift lever located?

options.text: In front of the left footrest.
In front of the right footrest.

questions.correctAnswerText: In front of the left footrest.
questions.explanation: The gear shift lever is in front of the left footrest. You operate it with your left foot. Lift your foot under the lever to shift to a higher gear. Press down to shift to a lower gear.

questions.question: When railroad tracks cross your lane at an angle, what is safest?

options.text: Ride straight across the tracks within your lane.
Riding straight across the tracks is dangerous.
It is not safe to cross tracks on a motorcycle.
Cross the tracks by riding on the road shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride straight across the tracks within your lane.
questions.explanation: When tracks cross at an angle, ride straight across while staying in your lane. Turning to cross at a 90-degree angle is dangerous because you might move into another lane.

questions.question: Why should motorcyclists in a group avoid riding in pairs?

options.text: A merging driver may not see both riders.
Helmet reflections may make it hard for riders to see.
Riding in pairs does not give riders enough space to move.
Left-side riders have difficulty exiting the highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riding in pairs does not give riders enough space to move.
questions.explanation: When riding in a group, motorcyclists should not ride side-by-side. Neither rider will have enough room to maneuver around hazards.

questions.question: What can help if your drive chain slips?
questions.explanation: If your chain slips, try tightening it. If that does not fix the problem, replace the chain before riding again.

questions.question: What is the best way to stop?

options.text: Grab the front brake lever hard.
Keep your knees against the tank and look ahead.
Apply more and more pressure to the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your knees against the tank and look ahead.
questions.explanation: For straight-line braking, apply the brakes smoothly and firmly. As weight shifts forward, the front wheel has more grip, so you can press the front brake harder while easing off the rear brake. Keep your knees against the tank and your eyes ahead to stay in a straight line.

questions.question: When you cannot avoid hitting an object or uneven surface, what should you do?

options.text: Lean the motorcycle to one side.
Rise up off the seat so your legs can absorb the impact.

questions.correctAnswerText: Rise up off the seat so your legs can absorb the impact.
questions.explanation: If you must ride over an obstacle or uneven surface, approach it as straight as possible. Slow down as much as you can and keep the motorcycle upright. Rise slightly off your seat so your knees can absorb some impact. Just before you hit it, roll the throttle slightly to lift the front wheel.

questions.question: When should you adjust your rearview mirror?
questions.explanation: Clean and adjust both mirrors before starting your motorcycle. Position them so you can see the lane behind you and as much of the side lane as possible.

questions.question: When riding at night compared to daytime, which should you NOT do?

options.text: Keep more distance between your motorcycle and other vehicles.
Use your high beam whenever possible.

questions.explanation: To stay safe at night, ride slower and stay farther behind other vehicles. Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see down the road better. Be ready to change your lane position, especially at night.

questions.question: A windshield:

options.text: Works as well as a face shield.
Does not fully protect your eyes from wind.
Should be used on windy days.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not fully protect your eyes from wind.
questions.explanation: A windshield does not provide the same protection as goggles or a face shield. Most windshields will not protect your eyes from wind.

questions.question: When securing a load, place it:

options.text: On only one side of the motorcycle.

questions.explanation: Keep loads low. Placing loads high can raise the motorcycle's center of gravity and affect balance. Spread loads evenly on both sides to prevent the bike from tilting.

questions.question: To reduce your chance of a crash, you should:

options.text: Keep other drivers from knowing your plans.
Always stay within one foot of another vehicle.

questions.explanation: Be visible at all times to reduce crash risk. Use signals and brake lights to show your plans. Keep space around your motorcycle and watch the road ahead, behind, and beside you.

questions.question: When should you use the front brake?

options.text: Every time you slow down or stop

questions.correctAnswerText: Every time you slow down or stop
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: When changing lanes, riders should:

options.text: Only use their mirrors to check for other vehicles.
Turn their head to look for traffic behind them.
Brake hard to let vehicles in blind spots pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn their head to look for traffic behind them.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots. Always turn your head to check for traffic before changing lanes.
